title: 1936 Prairie's verandah, tower and chimneys stand where its photograph puts them
items: The Thompson/Allerton house at 1936 Prairie: the winter photograph's camera is solved afresh. Its south-east corner is where the cornice turns nearest the lens, at the verandah's end, so the front reads verandah, tower, porch, stoop, as the 1911 map and the 1886 engraving draw it.

Through that camera the verandah runs about 7.6 m from the corner on three wider arches, and the tower, its door and the stoop's landing stand 2 m further north. The two south chimneys move to where the photograph shows them.
